candidates.quote: The P1 supported carriers up to 40Mhz, dual antennas and onboard video decoding and has been used in most DJI drones with Ocusync 2 and Ocusync 3. This includes Enterprise models and ground based DJI wireless products such as DJI Transmission.
The P1,S1 and S2 Chipsets are custom Asics used by DJI in their Ocusync based drones that are the basis for their Ocusync RF Wireless Link.
The new Mavic 3 again uses the P1 craft side, we know the RC-N1 that's used on the Mini2, Air 2/sand the M3 is based on the S1 however and is classed as Ocusync 2.

attempts.notes: No Mavic 3 Enterprise-specific teardown or chip-level source exists that I could open; the FCC internal photos (SS3-M3E2206) show boards but label no chips. The best evidence is that DJI's OcuSync link, including in Enterprise models and the Mavic 3 platform, runs on DJI's own custom P1/S-series ASIC modem, so both the module and its RF/radio chipset are in-house DJI (China). iFixit's Mavic 3 Pro chip ID hints at Maxscend LNAs and Skyworks front-end modules but only as 'likely' and for a different model, so I did not use it.
